sentences.text: This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3.
In this Writ Petition, the Petitioner has challenged the order dated 10.12.2024 passed by the learned 1st M.A.C.T., Jagatsinghpur in M.A.C. Case No.387 of 2015.

4. The brief facts of the case are that on 13.12.2002, at about 6.30 A.M., near Mohammadapur, on the Tarapur-Bilahat Public Bypass Road, the injured, who was engaged as a helper on a passenger bus bearing Registration No. OR-05-C-6929 which met with an accident while discharging his duties.

It is alleged that while he was loading luggage onto the said bus, a live electric wire came into contact with his neck, causing him to fall onto the road and sustain grievous fracture injuries to his left leg.
The accident is alleged to have occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the said bus.
5. he injured was initially shifted to the Government Hospital, Raghunathpur, and thereafter referred to S.C.B. Medical College and Hospital, Cuttack, for better treatment.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that the owner of the said bus had orally assured the injured that compensation would be paid through the Insurance Company.

However, it is contended that neither was any compensation paid nor did the owner extend cooperation to the injured in settlement of his claim, compelling the Petitioner to institute a claim petition before the Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation, Cuttack, which was registered as W.C. Case No.378-D/2003.
7.

Learned counsel further contends that the injured claimant thereafter filed a fresh claim application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 before the 1st Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-District Judge, Jagatsinghpur, claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.7,00,000/-
against the owner and the insurer of the offending bus.

entities.text: 1st Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-District Judge, Jagatsinghpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is stated that Kishorenagar Police furnished detailed information relating to the insurance particulars, as well as the name and address of the owner and other relevant documents, to the father of the injured to facilitate filing of the claim application before the competent Court.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner further argues that during trial the Insurance Company filed a petition before the Court of ADJ(2)-cum-M.A.C.T.,
Cuttack wherein vide order 24.09..2005 directed the Petitioner to furnish the insurance particulars before the court below for the purpose of enabling the insurance company to tress out the insurable interest of offending vehicle under Opposite Party No.2 at the time of alleged incident.

He further submits that the Petitioner challenging the order dated 24.09.2005 had filed Writ Petition vide W.P.(C) No.16056 of 2005 (Khulana Mahana vrs. Divisional Manager, United Insurance Co. Ltd.)
wherein it was held that if the Petitioner furnished the number of vehicle and date of accident the duty of insurance to verify and disclosed as to whether vehicle was insured with the Company on the date of accident or not.

entities.text: Khulana Mahana vrs. Divisional Manager, United Insurance Co. Ltd.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that, in the absence of specific policy particulars being furnished by the Petitioner, it was not possible for the Insurance Company to trace the relevant insurance policy pertaining to the offending bus.
It is, therefore, contended that the Petitioner ought to supply the requisite policy details of the said vehicle.

9. In view of the submissions advanced by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Petitioner, being a third party claimant, cannot reasonably be expected to be in possession of, or to procure, the insurance policy particulars of the offending vehicle.
The obligation to furnish such information primarily lies on the owner of the offending vehicle, and, where necessary, the insurer.
The learned Tribunal, therefore, ought to have exercised its statutory powers to secure the said particulars instead of directing the Petitioner to obtain the same.

10.This Court is of the view that the learned 1st Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jagatsinghpur,
should have invoked the powers conferred under Section 169 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, to call for the requisite insurance details either from the owner of the offending vehicle or from the Insurance Company.

In that view of the matter, the order dated 10.12.2024 passed by the learned 1st M.A.C.T., Jagatsinghpur, in M.A.C. Case No.387 of 2015, cannot be sustained and is accordingly set Bikram Biswal vs Divisional Manager New India on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135427480/
2 aside.

entities.text: Bikram Biswal vs Divisional Manager New India on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
11.The matter is remitted to the learned 1st M.A.C.T., Jagatsinghpur, with a direction to hear the case afresh, after obtaining the necessary insurance particulars in accordance with law, affording reasonable opportunity of hearing to the present Petitioner, and to pass a reasoned order within a period of three months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
10.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
